rituals.hook: Use Word Melt on Automatic-pattern blindness. Test this: Repeat the sound until the spell loses its language.
rituals.recognition_cue: Use Word Melt on Automatic-pattern blindness. Test this: Repeat the sound until the spell loses its language.

rituals.mission: Repeat the sound until the spell loses its language.

rituals.game_move: Start Choose Charged; use Listen Moment. Close with Return Seen.
rituals.unique_game_move: Start Choose Charged; use Listen Moment. Close with Return Seen.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Automatic habits & autopilot

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Repeat the sound until the spell loses its language.

GAME MOVE
Start Choose Charged; use Listen Moment. Close with Return Seen.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Charged — Choose one charged word—not a whole painful story.
2. Say Gently — Say it gently and steadily for about twenty seconds.
3. Listen Moment — Listen for the moment it becomes rhythm, mouth movement, or noise.
4. Stop Room — Stop there and look around the room.
5. Return Seen — Meaning may return; you have seen it separate once.

Word Melt lands here: repeat the sound until the spell loses its language. Leave at Return Seen.

rituals.title: SET THE CONVERSATION SIZE
rituals.name: SET THE CONVERSATION SIZE
rituals.hook: Set The Conversation Size gives Communication distortion a boundary. Keep the task narrow: A conversation can be important and still need a smaller container today.
rituals.recognition_cue: Set The Conversation Size gives Communication distortion a boundary. Keep the task narrow: A conversation can be important and still need a smaller container today.

rituals.game_move: Begin Read Bandwidth; hinge on Send Signal. Stopping line: Set Reopen.
rituals.unique_game_move: Begin Read Bandwidth; hinge on Send Signal. Stopping line: Set Reopen.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Communication & conflict

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
Set The Conversation Size gives Communication distortion a boundary. Keep the task narrow: A conversation can be important and still need a smaller container today.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A conversation can be important and still need a smaller container today.

GAME MOVE
Begin Read Bandwidth; hinge on Send Signal. Stopping line: Set Reopen.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Read Bandwidth — Choose your current safe bandwidth: ONE SENTENCE, THREE SENTENCES, or FULL CONVERSATION.
2. Choose Size — Name the purpose that must fit inside that size: acknowledge, request, pause, clarify, or repair.
3. Send Signal — Draft or say only the selected amount. Stop when the sentence limit is reached, even if more remains.
4. Set Reopen — Name when or under what condition the next level can reopen. If you cannot offer one, state that honestly without making a false promise.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
A conversation can be important and still need a smaller container today. When Set The Conversation Size reaches Set Reopen, leave it there.
rituals.formula_flow: Read Bandwidth → Choose Size → Send Signal → Set Reopen
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use bandwidth limits to conceal immediate danger, threats, abuse, medical urgency, or information another person needs for safety.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

HOOK

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Flashbacks need temporal translation.

GAME MOVE
Begin Alternate Lines; hinge on Keep Eyes. Close at Date Location; do not restart.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Alternate Lines — When memory body alarm begins, alternate lines: THEN—state one past fact; NOW—state one current difference.
2. Include Age — Include age, place, available help, bodily freedom, and exits.
3. Keep Eyes — Keep eyes open and touch the environment after every pair.
4. Date Location — The screen may replay; the subtitles restore date and location.

rituals.name: CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING
rituals.ritual_name: CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING
rituals.hook: Change One Thing, Watch One Feeling loosens Emotion blending. Keep this aim: Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.

rituals.game_move: Take Name Pair; keep Swap Variable literal. Let Tag Driver finish.
rituals.unique_game_move: Take Name Pair; keep Swap Variable literal. Let Tag Driver finish.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Urges, impulses & cravings

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Change One Thing, Watch One Feeling loosens Emotion blending. Keep this aim: Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.

GAME MOVE
Take Name Pair; keep Swap Variable literal. Let Tag Driver finish.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Name Pair — Name two emotions in the mixture and rate each with a simple low, medium, or high—not a number.
2. Hold Scene — Hold the scene steady. Choose only one variable to test: person, time, place, audience, or outcome.
3. Swap Variable — Imagine that one variable changed for ten seconds. Keep every other fact the same.
4. Tag Driver — Notice which emotion moved and which stayed. Tag the changed variable as a likely driver, not a final explanation.

FINISH MOVE — Complete Tag Driver, then return to your day.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Change One Thing, Watch One Feeling earns its finish: two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them. End with Tag Driver.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Pair → Hold Scene → Swap Variable → Tag Driver
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use imagined substitutions to rewrite trauma, deny facts, or continue once the scene becomes overwhelming or unreal.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

TRIGGER
Catastrophic prediction

about 1 minute

HOOK
Make Fear Name A Deadline contains Probability overestimation for a minute. Target: A warning must become testable before it can command you.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A warning must become testable before it can command you.

GAME MOVE
Keep Pin Forecast small; move through Score Odds. Endpoint: Update Odds.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Pin Forecast — Restate the fear as one visible or audible forecast—not a vague catastrophe.
2. Set Clock — Give the forecast a real time window.
3. Score Odds — Set confidence from 0 to 100 before checking anything.
4. Observe Safely — Use only a naturally occurring safe observation; never manufacture a test.
5. Update Odds — Hold the result and update confidence in either direction.

HOOK

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.

GAME MOVE
Begin Read Channels; no side task before Move Dial. Do not pass Check Panel.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Read Channels — Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use low, medium, or high.
2. Pick Smallest — Choose the safest channel with the lowest intensity. Do not pick the loudest one.
3. Move Dial — Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness.
4. Check Panel — Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are.

FINISH MOVE — Complete Check Panel, then return to your day.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move. Once visible, Disassemble The Alarm Panel can end at Check Panel.
rituals.formula_flow: Read Channels → Pick Smallest → Move Dial → Check Panel
rituals.safety:

4. Check Panel — Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are.

FINISH MOVE — Complete Check Panel, then return to your day.

The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move. Once visible, Disassemble The Alarm Panel can end at Check Panel.

GAME MOVE
Imagine Three Boxes to Do Not Force Forgiveness; no rewind. Act From Choice lands; leave it.

1. Imagine Three Boxes — Imagine three boxes: WHAT THEY DID; WHAT I LEARNED; WHAT I CHOOSE NOW.

4. Act From Choice — Take one action from the third box.

rituals.unique_game_move: Name Task to Remove Feature; no rewind. Build Smallest ends the useful part.

TRIGGER

HOOK

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Perfection should not be allowed to cancel function.

GAME MOVE
Name Task to Remove Feature; no rewind. Build Smallest ends the useful part.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Name Task — Name the task’s essential purpose.
2. Remove Feature — Remove every feature not required for that purpose.
3. Build Smallest — Build the smallest deliverable that still works, submit or finish it, then upgrade only if time and value justify the addition.

FINISH MOVE — Let Build Smallest be enough.

rituals.hook: The Room Has Jobs, Not Demands gives Action avoidance less space. Use this target: A room becomes lighter when objects return to jobs instead of accusations.

rituals.game_move: Use Scan Objects; stay concrete through Drop Demands. Exit at Choose Helper.
rituals.unique_game_move: Use Scan Objects; stay concrete through Drop Demands. Exit at Choose Helper.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
The Room Has Jobs, Not Demands gives Action avoidance less space. Use this target: A room becomes lighter when objects return to jobs instead of accusations.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A room becomes lighter when objects return to jobs instead of accusations.

GAME MOVE
Use Scan Objects; stay concrete through Drop Demands. Exit at Choose Helper.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Scan Objects — Choose four safe visible objects without moving toward them. Avoid screens if they add strain.
2. Name Jobs — For each object, name only its ordinary job: chair supports, lamp lights, cup holds, door opens.
3. Drop Demands — Say ‘not needed now’ to every function that does not serve the current safe moment. Do not remove or organise anything.
4. Choose Helper — Choose the one object whose real function supports the next action, then use only that function.

FINISH MOVE — Let Choose Helper be enough.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
The useful residue of The Room Has Jobs, Not Demands: a room becomes lighter when objects return to jobs instead of accusations. Stop with Choose Helper.
rituals.formula_flow: Scan Objects → Name Jobs → Drop Demands → Choose Helper
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop for visual pain, dizziness, nausea, disorientation, compulsive scanning, or any real emergency requiring immediate action.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

30–60 seconds

HOOK
When Action avoidance appears, choose Find Your Working Gear. Stay here: Motivation can guess; one work pulse can measure.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Motivation can guess; one work pulse can measure.

GAME MOVE
At Run Pulse, begin. Around Read Strain, notice. End when Set Gear completes.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Run Pulse — Choose one ordinary task and run it for exactly thirty seconds without trying to finish it.
2. Full Stop — Stop completely for fifteen seconds. Hands off, eyes away, and no planning the next move.
3. Read Strain — Rate actual strain as light, workable, heavy, or stop. Compare it with what you predicted before starting.
4. Set Gear — Choose the next gear—30/15, 60/30, or stop—and complete exactly one more cycle at that ratio.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Find Your Working Gear becomes real when: motivation can guess; one work pulse can measure. No second proof after Set Gear.
rituals.formula_flow: Run Pulse → Full Stop → Read Strain → Set Gear

Let task feedback lead while self-opinion becomes background sound.

rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Skill — Choose one familiar, low-risk task with clear external feedback.

3. Demote Voice — When self-commentary appears, let it continue faintly at the edge without answering or silencing it.
4. Finish Unit — Finish one complete task unit using feedback—not self-opinion—to make corrections.

rituals.name: ROTATE THE OBSERVATION DECK
rituals.hook: At Observer loss, reach for Rotate The Observation Deck. Stay here: Every viewpoint edits what becomes prominent.
rituals.recognition_cue: At Observer loss, reach for Rotate The Observation Deck. Stay here: Every viewpoint edits what becomes prominent.
rituals.goal: Every viewpoint edits what becomes prominent.
rituals.mission: Every viewpoint edits what becomes prominent.

rituals.unique_game_move: Observe Moment gets first beat; Spot Amplifier is pivot. End when Choose Position completes.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Observer loss & cognitive fusion

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
At Observer loss, reach for Rotate The Observation Deck. Stay here: Every viewpoint edits what becomes prominent.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Every viewpoint edits what becomes prominent.

GAME MOVE
Observe Moment gets first beat; Spot Amplifier is pivot. End when Choose Position completes.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Observe Moment — Observe the same moment from three positions: body-centred, environment-centred, and whole-field.
2. Spot Amplifier — Keep what each amplifies and hides.
3. Choose Position — Choose the position best suited to the next task rather than declaring any one neutral.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Rotate The Observation Deck is useful if: every viewpoint edits what becomes prominent. No second proof after Choose Position.

Use a stable perspective when rotation increases dissense of where you are.

rituals.play_the_loop:

2. Catch Bare — Catch the first bare instant before ‘cup,’ ‘cold,’ ownership, or preference appears.
3. Don't Freeze — Do not freeze it; simply recognise the order: contact, then concept.
4. Repeat Sound — Repeat with a sound.

HOOK
Move The Rule Between Worlds puts Context neglect on pause. Keep the lens here: A rule must survive context before it earns the word universal.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A rule must survive context before it earns the word universal.

GAME MOVE
One pass: State Rule through Compare Effects. Finish Keep Core; skip rechecking.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. State Rule — Picture the rule without naming who taught it.
2. Change Context — Place it in three contrasting settings—for example family, workplace, and friendship—with different power and consequences.
3. Compare Effects — Compare who is protected, restricted, or harmed in each setting.
4. Keep Core — Keep only the part that remains ethical and workable across contexts; Notice the rest as conditional.

FINISH MOVE — Complete Keep Core, then return to your day.

Sufficiency can coexist with ambition.

3. Choose Non — From this base, choose one non-desperate improvement.

FINISH MOVE — Choose Non closes the round.

Identify Part → Receive Adequacy → Choose Non

items.play_the_loop:
1. Pin Forecast — Restate the fear as one visible or audible forecast—not a vague catastrophe.

4. Observe Safely — Use only a naturally occurring safe observation; never manufacture a test.
5. Update Odds — Hold the result and update confidence in either direction.

items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Panic & body alarm

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
Meet Body alarm escalation with Disassemble The Alarm Panel. Work toward: The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.

GAME MOVE
Begin Read Channels; no side task before Move Dial. Do not pass Check Panel.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Read Channels — Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use low, medium, or high.
2. Pick Smallest — Choose the safest channel with the lowest intensity. Do not pick the loudest one.
3. Move Dial — Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness.
4. Check Panel — Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are.

FINISH MOVE — Complete Check Panel, then return to your day.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move. Once visible, Disassemble The Alarm Panel can end at Check Panel.
items.formula_flow: Read Channels → Pick Smallest → Move Dial → Check Panel
items.safety:
PAUSE
New, severe, or unusual physical symptoms require medical assessment. Stop for pain, faintness, breathing difficulty, confusion, or loss of orientation.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

Action fails when stimulation and state are badly paired.

GAME MOVE
Read Body to Select Work; no rewind. Stopping line: Reassess.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Read Body — Read current body alarm as low, medium, or high.
2. Select Work — Select work with matching demand: energising movement for low, steady production for medium, simple contained tasks for high.
3. Reassess — Reassess after one unit and change lanes if needed.

FINISH MOVE — Reassess is your cue to stop.

items.trigger_play_time:

HOOK

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A boundary can close one door without burning down the whole house.

GAME MOVE
Name Contact opens; Lower One changes the angle. Let Hold Setting finish.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Name Contact — Name the contact pattern you want to change without judging the person.
2. Pick Door — Choose exactly one access door: TIME, TOPIC, CHANNEL, LOCATION, or FREQUENCY.
3. Lower One — Lower that door by one clear level: shorter call, one topic excluded, text only, public place, or fewer contacts.
4. Hold Setting — State the new setting and leave every other door unchanged for this round.

WIN SIGNAL
A boundary can close one door without burning down the whole house. In Turn Down One Door, Not The Whole House, Hold Setting is the exit.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

TRIGGER

HOOK
The Room Has Jobs, Not Demands gives Action avoidance less space. Use this target: A room becomes lighter when objects return to jobs instead of accusations.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A room becomes lighter when objects return to jobs instead of accusations.

GAME MOVE
Use Scan Objects; stay concrete through Drop Demands. Exit at Choose Helper.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Scan Objects — Choose four safe visible objects without moving toward them. Avoid screens if they add strain.
2. Name Jobs — For each object, name only its ordinary job: chair supports, lamp lights, cup holds, door opens.
3. Drop Demands — Say ‘not needed now’ to every function that does not serve the current safe moment. Do not remove or organise anything.
4. Choose Helper — Choose the one object whose real function supports the next action, then use only that function.

FINISH MOVE — Let Choose Helper be enough.

1. Run Pulse — Choose one ordinary task and run it for exactly thirty seconds without trying to finish it.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Global meaning may be unavailable; today’s significance can still exist.

GAME MOVE
Keep order: Find Anchor, then Name Reason. Stop at Invest Time.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Find Anchor — Search only within the next twenty-four hours for one person, place, promise, task, or act that matters.
2. Name Reason — Name why it matters locally.
3. Invest Time — Give it ten minutes of undivided behaviour.

FINISH MOVE — Let Invest Time be enough.

items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Boundaries & over-responsibility

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

HOOK
At Boundary confusion, reach for Where Exactly Is The Observer?. Target: Test whether the witness has a fixed address.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Test whether the witness has a fixed address.

GAME MOVE
Search Carefully gets first beat; Observe Found is pivot. Endpoint: Rest Inability.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Search Carefully — Search carefully for the boundary, size, and location of the one who observes.
2. Check Behind — Check behind the eyes, chest, head, and surrounding field.
3. Observe Found — Every found sensation is itself observed.
4. Rest Inability — Rest with the inability to locate a final point.

Do not continue if location inquiry provokes feeling unreal or detached from yourself.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

items.unique_game_move: Choose Skill gets first beat; Demote Voice is pivot. Finish Unit lands; leave it.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Attention & cognitive overload

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
At Tunnel vision, reach for Put The Commentator In The Cheap Seat. One job: Let task feedback lead while self-opinion becomes background sound.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Let task feedback lead while self-opinion becomes background sound.

GAME MOVE
Choose Skill gets first beat; Demote Voice is pivot. Finish Unit lands; leave it.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Skill — Choose one familiar, low-risk task with clear external feedback.
2. Centre Feedback — Put sight, touch, sound, or the work result in the centre of attention.
3. Demote Voice — When self-commentary appears, let it continue faintly at the edge without answering or silencing it.
4. Finish Unit — Finish one complete task unit using feedback—not self-opinion—to make corrections.

FINISH MOVE — Let Finish Unit be enough.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Put The Commentator In The Cheap Seat is useful if: let task feedback lead while self-opinion becomes background sound. Let Finish Unit be enough.
items.formula_flow: Choose Skill → Centre Feedback → Demote Voice → Finish Unit
items.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if divided attention reduces accuracy or makes the activity unsafe.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

GOAL
Every viewpoint edits what becomes prominent.

GAME MOVE
Observe Moment gets first beat; Spot Amplifier is pivot. End when Choose Position completes.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Observe Moment — Observe the same moment from three positions: body-centred, environment-centred, and whole-field.
2. Spot Amplifier — Keep what each amplifies and hides.
3. Choose Position — Choose the position best suited to the next task rather than declaring any one neutral.
items.win_reward:

Rotate The Observation Deck is useful if: every viewpoint edits what becomes prominent. No second proof after Choose Position.

Use a stable perspective when rotation increases dissense of where you are.

1. Score Option — Score each option on value alignment, downside, reversibility, and learning.
2. Add Sentence — Add a sentence explaining every score.
3. Compare Patterns — Compare patterns rather than relying on the total alone.
4. Prefer Option — Prefer the option whose risk can be contained while important value is expressed.

FINISH MOVE — Let Prefer Option be enough.

items.plain:
FOUR-CELL DECISION MATRIX

TRIGGER
Emotional reasoning

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
Four-Cell Decision Matrix puts Emotion–fact confusion on pause. Aim: Separate value from danger before emotion blends them.

GOAL
Separate value from danger before emotion blends them.

GAME MOVE
One pass: Score Option through Compare Patterns. Stop at Prefer Option.

1. Score Option — Score each option on value alignment, downside, reversibility, and learning.
2. Add Sentence — Add a sentence explaining every score.
3. Compare Patterns — Compare patterns rather than relying on the total alone.
4. Prefer Option — Prefer the option whose risk can be contained while important value is expressed.

FINISH MOVE — Let Prefer Option be enough.

WIN SIGNAL
Four-Cell Decision Matrix closes with Prefer Option; what matters is separate value from danger before emotion blends them.

FORMULA FLOW
Score Option → Add Sentence → Compare Patterns → Prefer Option
